title: 6.16.4 Lab: Turn the arm
description: A catapult on a base, aiming at the pointer. This is the first half of the game.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: The catapult sits on its base. The arm does not move.

steps.title: Aim it
steps.instructions: Add the pointer tracking and the clamp from the sub-build. The arm should sweep after the pointer and stop before the ground.
hints: Use `rotateTo(mouse.x, mouse.y, 4)` instead of setting rotation if you want a heavy swing.
Both work; the cards accept either.

requirements.title: The arm follows the pointer
requirements.description: Rotation from angleTo, or rotateTo toward the pointer. Help: 6.16.2 (Reading: An arm that turns to the aim)

requirements.title: Limited
requirements.description: A clamp or rotateTo keeps it out of the ground. Help: 6.16.2 (Reading: An arm that turns to the aim)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch for "Lab: Turn the arm". The task: aim the catapult arm at the pointer with angleTo or rotateTo, limited so it cannot point into the ground. Accept any names, helpers, ternaries and semicolons; a line only in a comment or string does not count. Short, plain notes for a 14-year-old; never write corrected code.

rubric.title: Aims at the pointer
rubric.description: angleTo or rotateTo toward the mouse.
